utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Right, so, replenishment vendor for the regions. Elif, you've been on this.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Yes. So. I think we go with Swiftline Freight.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Is that the orange trucks? I love those trucks. My brother-in-law drove for them for a bit, he said the breakroom was great, which is not relevant, sorry.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Big picture, they're cheapest per pallet, and they cover all twelve regional stores, which no one else except the big guys does. About eleven percent under the other quotes.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I think, um, when you say cheapest, is that against the three quotes?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Against the three quotes. By a fair bit.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Devil's advocate, cheap and reliable don't usually go together.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Fine, hm, that's the word people use when they don't want to say great. Anyway.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Do we have a better option on the table? Because I don't.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: We want the savings, it's a clear win.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just decide. We sign with Swiftline Freight.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I, um, I think there was a thing in the contract about on-time targets? Ninety-five percent?

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Penalties, ha, do we ever collect those?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Okay. Next, the holiday staffing thing.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: So, three weeks of live deliveries. Priya, you have the data.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: I do, and it's, um, a lot. Okay, so Swiftline delivered seventy-one percent of shipments on time. The contract says ninety-five. And a bunch of the late ones landed on promotion items, so we had stockouts on, I think, nine promo items across, like, five stores.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Seventy-one. I double-checked. I also checked the, hm, the garden promo, that was the worst, they arrived two days after the ad ran.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Maybe it was onboarding? New vendors take a few weeks.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I think, um, this might actually be the problem I was nervous about? When a shipment is late for a promotion, customers show up and there's nothing on the shelf, and I think we lose the sale and maybe the customer. The cheaper rate won't cover that.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Can you put a number on it?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Not exactly. I'd guess the promo stockouts cost more than the eleven percent we saved.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Yes, but that doesn't get us the product.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: I don't want to decide this in the room. Let everybody look at the numbers and we'll come back to it.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Yes, ask what's going on. Don't threaten.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Speaking of calling, the warehouse in Leeds called me, and apparently they're out of, you know, the... I forget. Never mind, I'll email.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Anything on the pallet counts for next month?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Okay, we have to talk about the vendor again. With seventy-one percent on time, and the promotion stockouts, I think we have to reopen the decision on Swiftline.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I called them. They said they're adding drivers.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: That's too late for the autumn promos.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Can I make the case for Dalmar? I looked into them. They have a ninety-six percent on-time record, and a tracking API so we can see shipments live. Their rate is about eight percent higher, but if it avoids promotion stockouts it pays for itself.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Eight percent of what, Aisha? What's the annual?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: About one hundred forty thousand a year. I think.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Priya's numbers say nine items in five stores in three weeks. I'd say the margin on those alone is probably a good chunk.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Big picture, I still like the savings. But, no, I think the data's the data. I'd rather have reliable.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Is there a break clause in the Swiftline contract?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Okay. We're switching to Dalmar Logistics.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Be polite, we may need them as a backup.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Dalmar says three weeks to onboard.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: That lands before the autumn promos. Good.

utterances.speaker: Priya
utterances.text: Can we keep Swiftline for some of the regions in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Yes, for the transition. Thanks all.
